Replay

Replay authoring tools

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Installation and project contractIsolated previewsCanonical Scrapyard example

Use the optional Godot editor panel to run a project's authoring commands and inspect their validation results. The tools require explicit gameplay policy and operate outside a live match. Scrapyard is the complete worked example; model, extractors and validation remain Odin. The small EditorPlugin/preview controls use GDScript for normal Godot UI.

Installation and project contract#

A project opts in with replay_authoring.json:

JSON
{
  "worker": "res://tools/authoring.py",
  "ability": "res://data/abilities/salvefield.tres",
  "workbench": "res://dev/ability_workbench.tscn"
}

The normal build/build_scripts.sh PROJECT installs the addon when this file is present. Enable res://addons/replay_authoring/plugin.cfg in project settings (Scrapyard already does). Installation writes local framework/Python toolchain paths; re-run it when relocating the project/toolchain. It does not install tools or send anything to external services. Current process/job helpers target native macOS/Linux authoring with Python and an Odin build environment. If Odin is not on PATH, the example worker can enter the framework's Nix environment.

The panel supplies Validate/Bake tools, current/stale content status, clickable issues, Resource selection, workbench/scenario actions and feature drafts. The project worker accepts project/framework/Godot/result paths, an action and optional selection/name/kind/latency arguments. It publishes an atomic JSON result with ok, running, message, issues, optional stale and retained log paths. Issues contain source, path, message and optionally a source line. Source links open Resources, scenes or scripts through the editor's normal interfaces.

Save & Validate/Bake saves open scenes and the selected saved Resource. Save other edited Resources before running a project-wide action. The worker builds current Odin code and runs typed checks in a separate bounded process. View validation instantiates authored scenes there, outside the live game's World. Their scripts can still run construction/ready code, so use view scenes whose initialization is appropriate for isolated validation.

jobs.py supplies bounded process-group ownership, per-stage logs, cancellation files and atomic result publication. UI waits are nonblocking. Cancellation and failure retain logs and prevent incomplete content publication. The existing artifact exporter still checks source/build provenance before replacing data; --check detects interrupted artifact/receipt replacement. Process cleanup ignores missing/dead groups but still signals a live owned parent if group signalling fails.

Isolated previews#

preview_controls.gd is a reusable CanvasLayer controller for Node2D previews. A preview implements preview_refresh, preview_apply(phase, fraction, speed), preview_radius and optionally preview_range, preview_phase, preview_message and preview_can_refresh. The controller offers idle/attack/charge/hurt/death, scrubbing, 0–4× playback and radius/range guides. It reloads authored resources before explicit refresh; live-bound enemy views refuse refresh before reloading.

Scrapyard copies validated gameplay display values. Enemy previews also own a validated appearance Resource copy, so invalid frame/texture/timing edits preserve the last valid display. Child charge animation follows the preview playback rate. These clocks/Resources stay outside World. An ability preview depicts its configured area/status; actual hits, healing, cooldowns and replay behavior are tested in the isolated encounter and scenario runner.

Canonical Scrapyard example#

See the walkthrough. It covers Resource-based status references, shared checked extraction, a complete Salvefield workflow, authored player-character appearances, draft scaffolding with stable IDs that does not replace existing files, recording verification, and local peers. Actor drafts preserve the game's existing root binding and compose a generated visual child; rules and feature assertions remain explicit TODOs. Drafts do not enter the stock catalog automatically.

The UI uses the same commands as CI, including the existing recording verifier and replay/testing correction/takeover helpers. In-memory checkpoint comparison does not claim to test transport/security/lease failure. The network command runs real local peers under the chosen latency profile; the framework's separate host-crash fixture remains available for full migration testing.
